title: Opening
sentences: The best waste is the waste we never create.
Jai Hind, respected judges.
I am Avni Choudhary from Class 6, and my model is on Clean India Mission and Waste Management.
A beautiful India is not made only with beautiful buildings and roads, but with clean surroundings and responsible people.
Every day, we throw away plastic, paper and food peels.
But — where does all this waste go?

title: Clean India Mission
sentences: The Clean India Mission, or Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, was launched on 2 October 2014 by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, on Mahatma Gandhi ji's birth anniversary.
In Phase 1, the goal was to make India open defecation free.
In Phase 2, the goal is ODF Plus: to keep that status, and to manage solid and liquid waste.

title: Smart city & the hydrogen train
sentences: This is my smart city, with green energy to reduce carbon emissions.
The solar panels on the houses use energy from the sun, and this charging station charges the electric car with solar electricity.
This is India's first hydrogen train.
It was flagged off on 17 July 2026, and it runs about 89 kilometres, from Jind to Sonipat in Haryana.
It gives out no smoke — only water vapour and heat.

title: Plastic roads & the rain garden
sentences: This is Professor Rajagopalan Vasudevan, the Plastic Man of India.
He showed how waste plastic can help build roads, and he got the Padma Shri in 2018.
Next to the road is my rain garden.
It soaks up rainwater from roofs and roads, reduces flooding and helps refill the groundwater.

title: Clean water, rivers & Ganesha
sentences: This is my wastewater treatment plant.
Dirty water is cleaned in layers: stones stop leaves and packets, charcoal removes the smell, and cotton traps fine dirt.
The water comes out clearer, but a real plant also removes germs before it goes back to a river.
Here in Gorakhpur, people cleaned Ram Ghat on the Rapti river, and sent about 170 kilos of plastic and other waste for recycling.
Rivers are not dustbins.
My eco-friendly Ganesha is made of clay and pulses.
Unlike Plaster of Paris, the clay breaks down easily in water, and the pulses are natural and biodegradable.

title: Waste segregation & the 7Rs
sentences: Now, waste segregation: separating waste where it is made.
Wet waste, like peels, becomes compost or biogas.
Dry waste, like plastic, paper, metal and glass, can be recycled.
Mixed waste becomes garbage; separated waste becomes a resource.
And the 7Rs, like Refuse, Reduce and Reuse, help us make less waste.

title: Biogas village
sentences: In my village, this biogas plant takes wet waste, cow dung and water.
Bacteria break it down without oxygen, and make methane and carbon dioxide.
This biogas is used for cooking and for electricity, like the light in this hut.

title: Waste to energy
sentences: Single-use plastic is hard to recycle.
In a waste-to-energy plant, waste that cannot be recycled is burnt in a closed chamber with pollution control.
The heat makes steam, the steam spins a turbine, and we get electricity.
But we must never burn plastic in the open.
Another way is eco-bricks: plastic bottles packed tightly with clean, dry plastic, used to build benches and small walls.

title: Best out of waste
sentences: My Swachh Bharat waste collector shows the machines that clean our roads.
I made it from old toy-car tyres, a motor, a light and cardboard.
My wall hanging is made from spoons, bangles and pistachio shells.
Waste can be used in many ways.

title: Conclusion
sentences: I do not want to define my India by its waste.
I want to define its beauty by the way it reduces, reuses and recycles, and uses green energy.
The best waste is the waste we never create.
Thank you. Jai Hind! Jai Bharat!
